doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Early piano lessons in Halifax and getting the movie-theatre job
summary: Budd's classical lessons and conservatory, quitting high school at 13, and his father arranging a movie-house piano job.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My math isn’t quite up to snuff. And when you were a young man, what kind of music was the music of the day?

I had classical music piano lessons. I went to a neighbor who was a piano teacher and subsequent teachers and just learned to play music, and then finally went to the Conservatory in Halifax. They had young ladies mostly who were studying and you would employ one of them to teach you at good rates I guess, and you’d have one for a year and then she would go on to the next grade and I’d get another one. But I got the same thing again. So I learned how to read, how to put fingering into exercises, and how to memorize, but nothing about anything about tone or quality or things like that. And I got to be very good at it because you do it in a practice stall. After, when I became 13, my mother said maybe high school may be a little too much for you. that and said I think it is, I’ve had enough. So we quit. I took two years, I went to high school and in a couple of years there was a show put on and they had some people to play music, and there was not a piano player maybe. They got me to play and I began to play, and learned tunes like that. The birds are singing/I’ll feather your nest and songs like that. And all these old, old songs that day. And then when I went into college I was looking for a job and my father one day was walking down the street, I had a job one year working at City Hall working as a filing clerk in my first year in college, and at the first intermission after that Dad said to me walking down the street, “I think you could probably play the piano in a moving picture theater.” And I was shocked. I thought he doesn’t know anything about music and he’s dreaming. So he asked the manager if he would be interested and he said “come down and see me.” He come in and he listened to me and said “come down this afternoon” — this is Thursday— “and finish out this week and if you do all right we’ll hire you.” And at that time I had read Horatio Alger stories — you ever heard of him?
